Pistolero:
P: Gunslinger Subclass: Fire Six-Shooters with Incredible Speed

FIGURE: MARIYA SVIRIDOVA

P: Bullets are power, and you have long believed that more bullets equal more power. Your expertise is in delivering a hail of deadly fire to pulverize your enemies. Not every bullet needs to be accurate to make a difference.

H4: Level 3: Close-Quarters Shooting

P: Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn’t impose Disadvantage on your attack rolls with Ranged weapons.

H4: Level 3: Fan the Hammer [Maneuver]

P: When you take the Attack action with a Ranged weapon that doesn’t have the Two-Handed property, you can expend one Risk Die as a Bonus Action to make two additional ranged attacks with that weapon. These additional attacks always have Disadvantage, regardless of circumstance. You can’t use the Automatic mastery property with these attacks, and you must have a free hand to use this maneuver.

H4: Level 6: Disarm

P: When you score a Critical Hit and trigger your Gut Shot feature against a creature, you can disarm the target instead of lodging a projectile in it. The target drops one object of your choice that it’s holding, with the object landing in a space of your choice up to 15 feet away from the target.

H4: Level 10: Showdown [Maneuver]

P: When you roll Initiative, you can expend one Risk Die to draw a Ranged weapon and make an attack using it. Add the Risk Die to the damage roll. On a hit, the target has Disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you on the first round of combat.

H4: Level 14: Bullet Time

P: Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged attack using a weapon, you can gain Advantage on the roll.
College of Masks:
P: Bard Subclass: Embody Archetypal Characters Through Theater Masks

P: Bards in the College of Masks are virtuoso performers who practice becoming the figures they portray, rather than merely imitating them. Bards who join in this college subscribe to the notion that all life is performed in a “Great Play,” and that all people wear metaphorical masks at all times. To engage in this great stage drama, a masked Bard carries a number of Persona Masks, each bestowing the powers of a specific theatrical figure.

FIGURE: LUCAS FERREIRA CM

H4: Level 3: Persona Masks

P: You learn to create magical masks, each of which allows you to take on a different persona and gain some aspect of that archetypal character.

P: Persona Masks. You gain 3 masks of your choice from the “Persona Masks” section later in this subclass’s description. You gain an additional mask at Bard level 6 (4 masks) and Bard level 14 (5 masks). You can exchange one of your masks for another one whenever you finish a Long Rest.

P: Wearing a Mask. You can put on a mask or switch the mask you are wearing as a Bonus Action. Only you can gain the effects of your masks.

P: Replacing a Mask. If one of your masks is lost or stolen, you can remake the mask over the course of 8 hours, which can be done during a Long Rest.

H4: Level 3: Thespian

P: Your theatrical talents grant you the following benefits.

P: Disguise Kits. You gain proficiency with the Disguise Kit.

P: Dramatic Flair. Whenever you make a Charisma (Performance) check, add your Bardic Inspiration die to the roll without expending it.

H4: Level 6: Virtuoso Skill

P: Once per turn when you make a D20 Test, you can choose to make it with Charisma if the test doesn’t use it already.

P: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

H4: Level 14: Master of Many Faces

P: You can wear two masks simultaneously, gaining the benefits of both.

H4: Persona Masks

P: The following masks are listed alphabetically.

P: Angel. This flawless alabaster mask depicts a serene Celestial. Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature with an attack or spell, you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal extra Radiant damage to the target equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die.

P: Archmage. This clay mask topped with a pointed hat bears the wrinkles of a cantankerous archmage. When you reach a Bard level specified in the following table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared while you wear this mask.

DIV: Archmage Persona Spells
Bard Level	Spells
3	Fire Bolt, Scorching Ray, Thunderwave
5	Lightning Bolt
7	Ice Storm
9	Wall of Stone

FIGURE: LUCAS FERREIRA CM

P: Devil. This obsidian mask bears the fangs and horns of a handsome fiend. When you take damage from a creature that is within 30 feet of yourself, you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration as a Reaction to deal Fire damage to the creature. This damage equals two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die, and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the damage dealt.

P: Dragon. When you put on this mask, and as a Bonus Action on each of your turns while you wear it, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die to exhale flames in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in the Cone makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Fire damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die, or half as much damage on a successful save.

P: Faceless. Two perfectly round eyeholes stare out of this otherwise featureless porcelain mask. While you wear this mask, you always have the Disguise Self spell prepared. Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn’t require a spell slot. If you do so, the spell’s casting time becomes 1 minute for that casting and its duration becomes 8 hours. The spell ends early if you remove this mask.

P: Gladiator. This grim metal helm, pockmarked and scratched, conceals the entire face. While you wear this mask, you have proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Shields. As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration to make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

P: Hierophant. In lieu of a face, this bronze mask bears the image of a holy symbol, with the barest of slits to see through. When you reach a Bard level specified in the following table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared while you wear this mask.

DIV: Hierophant Persona Spells
Bard Level	Spells
3	Aid, Cure Wounds, Spare the Dying
5	Revivify
7	Death Ward
9	Mass Cure Wounds

P: Jester. This cloth mask of a grinning jester is adorned with bells and checkerboard patterns. When you put on this mask, and as a Bonus Action on each of your turns while you wear it, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You can also expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast Vicious Mockery as a part of this mask’s Bonus Action.

P: Noble. This gleaming silver mask has two rubies set into its eyesockets. You can use your Bardic Inspiration as a part of the Bonus Action to put on this mask. When a creature with your Bardic Inspiration die fails a D20 Test while you wear this mask, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die twice and add the higher result to the d20.
Dragon Domain:
P: Cleric Subclass: Channel the Might of Dragon Gods

P: While dragons are the foremost worshipers of the Dragon Domain, the draconic deities accept the worship of any who crave wealth or power. Clerics of the Dragon Domain, often considered cultists, can channel the power and aspect of dragons, unleashing fearsome elemental magic and manifesting the awe-inspiring presence of an ancient wyrm.

P: The principal gods of the Dragon Domain include Tiamat, the five-headed mother of chromatic dragons, and Bahamut, the just and wise god of metallic dragons.

H4: Level 3: Chromatic Affinity

P: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. When you cast a Cleric spell or use a Cleric feature that deals Necrotic or Radiant damage, you can change that damage to the chosen type.

P: Once per turn when you deal damage of the chosen damage type to a creature, you can deal extra damage of that type equal to your Cleric level to that creature. You can deal this extra damage a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

H4: Level 3: Dragon Domain Spells

P: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Dragon Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

DIV: Dragon Domain Spells
Cleric Level	Spells
3	Chromatic Orb, Command, Darkvision, Dragon’s Breath
5	Fly, Protection from Energy
7	Banishment, Charm Monster
9	Dominate Person, Summon Dragon

H4: Level 3: Draconic Majesty

P: As a Magic action, you can present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to manifest an aura of draconic authority around yourself in a 30-foot Emanation. Choose the Charmed or Frightened condition. Each creature of your choice in the Emanation must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the chosen condition for 1 minute. A creature Charmed or Frightened by this feature makes another Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

FIGURE: NOA KRIUKOVA

H4: Level 6: Wyrm’s Blessing

P: You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to cast Dragon’s Breath or Protection from Energy on yourself rather than expending a spell slot. When you cast either spell in this way, the spell doesn’t require Concentration. This spell ends early if you cast that spell again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die.

H4: Level 17: Legendary Aspect

P: By conjuring the wings, claws, or tail of an ancient dragon, you can take one of the following Legendary Actions immediately after another creature’s turn. Once you use this feature to take a Legendary Action, you can’t take that one again until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature three times and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore one use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

P: Rend. You move up to your Speed and cast a Cleric cantrip that has a casting time of an action or make one melee attack using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. The attack uses your Wisdom for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

P: Tail Swipe. Each Large or smaller creature you choose within 10 feet of you gains the Prone condition.

P: Wingbeat. You immediately move up to your Speed. During this movement, you have a Fly Speed up to your Speed and don’t provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Circle of the City:
P: Druid Subclass: Master the Urban Jungle

P: The Circle of the City draws its power from buildings, streets, and people. These “Urban Druids” make their homes in sprawling settlements, far from the domains of their wild brethren.

P: An Urban Druid’s magic can twist the city streets into knots and raise maze-like walls in alleyways. They might leap from rooftop to rooftop, commune with doors and walls for information, or transform into a rat to go unseen.

H4: Level 3: Circle of the City Spells

P: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the City Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

DIV: Circle of the City Spells
Druid Level	Spells
3	Grease, Jump, Shatter, Spider Climb
5	Meld into Stone, Sending
7	Fabricate, Stone Shape
9	Animate Objects, Passwall

H4: Level 3: City Shape

FIGURE: LUCAS FERREIRA CM

P: You can expend a use of your Wild Shape to cast Meld into Stone, Passwall, or Stone Shape without a spell slot.

H4: Level 3: Urban Druid

P: Your magic and skills are specialized for city life, granting you the following benefits.

P: Street Savvy. Choose Acrobatics, History, Intimidation, Investigation, Persuasion, or Stealth. You gain a bonus to checks using this skill equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1). You can change your selection when you finish a Long Rest.

P: Urban Magic. Your magic takes on the aesthetic trappings of the urban landscape. Spells like Entangle, Grasping Vine, Spike Growth, and Wall of Thorns might cause growths of cobblestones, twisting pipes, or broken glass. The spells Speak with Plants, Transport via Plants, and Tree Stride can target structures instead of plants.

H4: Level 6: Object Shape

P: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you can choose the form of an Animated Object created by the Animate Objects spell. You choose the object’s size (up to Large). At Druid level 10, you can also shape-shift into a Huge object.

H4: Level 10: Wall Warp

P: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you takes damage from an attack, you can take a Reaction to cast Wall of Stone between the target and the attacker. When you cast the spell in this way, you create a single 10-foot-by-10-foot panel that is 1 inch thick (AC 15, 30 HP, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage), which disappears at the end of your next turn. The panel takes the damage of the attack and disappears early if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

P: Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

H4: Level 14: Urban Colossus

P: While shape-shifted into an animated object, you gain the following benefits.

P: Armor Class. Until you leave the form, your AC equals 18.

P: Limited Damage Threshold. Once per turn when you take less than 10 damage from a single attack or effect, you can reduce that damage to 0.

P: Multiattack. You can use Slam twice when you take the Attack action.

P: Unstoppable. You can move through the space of any creature. Moving through its space doesn’t cost you extra movement, but you can’t stop in the same space. If the creature is your size or smaller, it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to 2d6 plus your Wisdom modifier and has the Prone condition when you enter its space. A creature can take this damage once per turn.
Beastborne:
P: Ranger Subclass: Channel Lycanthropic Fury

P: Whether by infected bite or insidious curse, your blood was infected with the magic of lycanthropy. A ferocious, bestial form lies just beneath your skin, awaiting the allure of blood and the thrill of a hunt. Perhaps, if you can avoid the violence or the siren call of moonlight, you can resist the lycanthropic urge. Or perhaps you might embrace the infection as a blessing or wield it as a fearsome weapon.

H4: Level 3: Lycanthrope

FIGURE: LUCAS FERREIRA CM

P: Your true form is a bestial hybrid, granting you the following benefits.

P: Claws. You have a set of vicious claws that you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes. When you deal damage with an Unarmed Strike, you can deal Slashing damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike’s normal damage.

P: Climb Speed. You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

P: Darkvision. You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

H4: Level 3: Bestial Aspect

P: In the throes of combat, you gradually lose control and slip into a beastlike form. The degree of your transformation is represented by your Bestial Aspect Level, which starts at 0. Your Bestial Aspect Level grants you benefits, as shown on the Bestial Aspect table. You gain all the benefits of your Bestial Aspect Level and lower.

P: When you deal damage to an enemy, you can take a Bonus Action to increase your Bestial Aspect Level by 1. If you don’t deal damage to an enemy for 1 minute, your Bestial Aspect Level resets to 0.

DIV: Bestial Aspect
Level	Benefits
0	—
1	Carnage. You gain a +2 bonus to your damage rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes.
2	Fast Movement. Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
3	Blood Frenzy. You have Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its Hit Points.
4	Thick Hide. If you aren’t wielding a Shield, you gain a +2 bonus to AC.
5	Retaliation. When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of yourself, you can take a Reaction to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

H4: Level 7: Feral Howl

P: When you roll Initiative, you can roll a d4 and increase your Bestial Aspect Level to the number rolled.

H4: Level 11: Bloodthirsty Fury

P: You have gained control over your bestial rage, granting you the following benefits.

P: Bestial Mark. You can cast Hunter’s Mark as a part of the Bonus Action to increase your Bestial Aspect Level.

P: Greater Carnage. The damage bonus of your Carnage benefit increases to +3.

H4: Level 15: Monstrous Resilience

P: Once per turn when you take damage, you can reduce the total damage you take, to a minimum of 0. The reduction equals your Constitution modifier plus your Bestial Aspect Level.
Magic Missile Mage:
P: Wizard Subclass: Cast Magic Missile Better Than Anyone

P: Magic Missile is a staple wizard spell, beloved for its versatility and unerring accuracy. As a Missile Mage, however, your fondness for the spell borders on obsession. Your studies focus entirely on this spell, exploring every aspect of its casting, resulting in new augmentations and greater power.

H4: Level 3: Magic Missile Savant

P: Add the Magic Missile spell to your spellbook for free. Your expertise in this spell grants you the following benefits.

P: Extra Darts. When you cast Magic Missile, you create an extra dart of magical force. You create two extra darts at Wizard level 6, three extra darts at Wizard level 10, and four extra darts at Wizard level 14.

P: Free Casting. You can cast Magic Missile without a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

P: Penetrating Darts. Your Magic Missile darts bypass any effect, such as the Shield spell, that specifically blocks the Magic Missile spell.

H4: Level 6: Versatile Missiles

P: You can accurately guide your Magic Missile darts to strike a target wherever you choose. When you cast Magic Missile, you can add one of the following Versatile Missile effects to a target struck by the darts. Each effect has a cost, which is the number of darts you must forgo to add the effect to the target. You can add different effects to different targets, paying the cost for each effect separately.

P: Trip Missile (Cost: 1 Dart). The target must succeed on Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Prone condition.

P: Blinding Missile (Cost: 3 Darts). The target must succeed on Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.

P: Stunning Missile (Cost: 5 Darts). The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn.

H4: Level 10: Shield of Missiles

P: When you cast Magic Missile, you can direct the darts in a tight orbit around yourself, creating a protective 10-foot Emanation originating from you, which lasts for up to 1 minute.

P: You gain a bonus to your Armor Class equal to the number of darts orbiting you (maximum bonus of +5). Whenever a creature within 120 feet misses you with an attack roll, one dart strikes the attacker, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you by one.

P: Whenever the Emanation enters the space of a creature you can see and whenever a creature you can see enters the Emanation or ends its turn there, you can strike the target with any number of darts orbiting you, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you. You can damage a creature with the Emanation only once per turn.

P: Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

H4: Level 14: Giga-Missile

P: When you cast Magic Missile, you can enhance the damage of the spell. You deal extra Force damage with each dart equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

P: Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).
